litellm.displayName: LiteLLM Provider for GitHub Copilot Chat
litellm.description: Use 100+ LLMs in GitHub Copilot Chat through your LiteLLM proxy: streaming, tool calling, vision, reasoning, and multiple servers. Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure, Ollama, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

litellm.provider.baseUrl.title: Base URL
litellm.provider.label.title: Label
litellm.provider.label.description: Optional label identifying the litellm-vscode-chat.servers entry this group mirrors. The extension's server sync sets it; it gives groups that share a base URL and credentials distinct identities.
litellm.provider.apiKey.title: API Key
litellm.provider.apiKey.description: LiteLLM API key. Leave empty for servers without authentication.
litellm.provider.oauthTokenUrl.title: OAuth Token URL
litellm.provider.oauthTokenUrl.descripti: OAuth2 token endpoint for client-credentials authentication, e.g. https://idp.example.com/oauth2/token. Set this together with the client ID to authenticate with a short-lived bearer token instead of a static API key.
litellm.provider.oauthClientId.title: OAuth Client ID
litellm.provider.oauthClientId.descripti: Client ID for the OAuth2 client-credentials grant. Required together with the token URL.
litellm.provider.oauthClientSecret.title: OAuth Client Secret
litellm.provider.oauthClientSecret.descr: Client secret for the OAuth2 client-credentials grant. Leave empty for public clients.
litellm.provider.oauthScopes.title: OAuth Scopes
litellm.provider.oauthScopes.description: Space-separated scopes to request with the token, e.g. "litellm.read litellm.write". Leave empty to request none.
litellm.provider.virtualKeyHeader.title: Virtual Key Header
litellm.provider.virtualKeyHeader.descri: Name of a custom header carrying a LiteLLM virtual key, e.g. x-litellm-api-key. Sent on every request to this server when both the header and its value are set.
litellm.provider.virtualKeyValue.title: Virtual Key Value
litellm.provider.virtualKeyValue.descrip: The virtual key sent in the header named above.

litellm.walkthrough.title: Get started with LiteLLM for Copilot Chat
litellm.walkthrough.description: Connect a LiteLLM server and use its models in GitHub Copilot Chat.
litellm.walkthrough.connectServer.title: Connect your LiteLLM server
litellm.walkthrough.connectServer.descri:
Add your server in the LiteLLM dashboard: enter a label, the base URL and, if your server needs one, an API key.
[Open the Dashboard](command:litellm.openDashboard)
litellm.walkthrough.pickModel.title: Pick a LiteLLM model in chat
litellm.walkthrough.pickModel.descriptio:
Open Copilot Chat and click the model picker at the bottom of the chat input. Models from your LiteLLM server are listed under the name you gave it.
[Open Copilot Chat](command:workbench.action.chat.open)
litellm.walkthrough.configureModel.title: Configure per-model options
litellm.walkthrough.configureModel.descr: Select a LiteLLM model that supports reasoning, then click the "Thinking Effort" label next to the model name in the chat input. "Provider default" sends nothing and leaves the choice to your provider.
litellm.walkthrough.verifyConnection.des:
Run a connection test to check every configured server and count the models it serves.
[Test Connection](command:litellm.testConnection)
litellm.walkthrough.fineTune.title: Fine-tune the extension
litellm.walkthrough.fineTune.description:
Timeouts, model list caching, prompt caching, custom headers, and per-model request parameters live in the extension settings.
[Open Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22@ext:vivswan.litellm-vscode-chat%22%5D)
litellm.walkthrough.generateCommit.title: Generate commit messages
litellm.walkthrough.generateCommit.descr:
Enable commit message generation and pick the model that drafts them; a sparkle button then appears in the Source Control title bar, and the command drafts a message from your staged changes into the commit box.
[Open Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22litellm-vscode-chat.commitGeneration%22%5D)
litellm.walkthrough.generatePr.title: Generate pull request descriptions
litellm.walkthrough.generatePr.descripti:
Enable pull request description generation and pick the model that drafts them; the command compares your branch against its base, then copies a drafted title and description to your clipboard.
[Open Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22litellm-vscode-chat.prGeneration%22%5D)
litellm.walkthrough.inlineCompletions.de:
Enable inline completions and pick a completions-capable (FIM) model; suggestions then appear as ghost text while you type, in whichever languages you allow.
[Open Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22litellm-vscode-chat.inlineCompletions%22%5D)
litellm.walkthrough.reviewComments.title: Get AI review comments
litellm.walkthrough.reviewComments.descr:
Enable review comments and pick the model that writes them; the review commands then read your uncommitted changes, or the file you are in, and leave comments on the lines they are about - which you can reply to.
[Open Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22litellm-vscode-chat.reviewComments%22%5D)
litellm.config.servers.description: LiteLLM servers, declared as settings. Machine-scoped: this lives in your user settings only (workspaces cannot override it, and Settings Sync does not carry it to other machines). Each entry syncs to a VS Code language-model provider group automatically, so servers can be managed here or in the LiteLLM dashboard. The `label` is the entry's identity: renaming it creates a new provider group, and removing an entry cannot remove its group (VS Code offers no API for that; to delete a leftover group, remove its object from the JSON array in the profile's `User/chatLanguageModels.json`, then reload the window). Secret-capable fields (`auth.apiKey`, `auth.oauth.clientSecret`, `auth.virtualKey.value`, the OAuth companions) may be written inline here - visible in settings files - or omitted and stored in VS Code secret storage instead, via the dashboard or the 'LiteLLM: Set Server Secret' command. Inline values take precedence over stored ones.
litellm.config.servers.label.description: Display name and identity of the server; the provider group is named after it.
litellm.config.servers.apiVersion.descri: What to append to the base URL: leave unset to auto-detect (keep a version segment already in the URL, else /v1); "" appends nothing; "v2" appends /v2.
litellm.config.servers.auth.description: How to authenticate to this server: exactly one of `apiKey` (bearer token, the common case), `oauth` (client credentials), or `virtualKey` (a key in a custom header). Omit entirely for servers that need no credentials. The `apiKey` form may carry a sibling `virtualKey` companion for gateways that check both headers; more than one form is reported as misconfigured and the entry is not used until fixed.
litellm.config.servers.auth.apiKey.descr: LiteLLM API key, sent as an Authorization bearer plus an X-API-Key copy, inline. Omit to keep it in secret storage instead.
litellm.config.servers.auth.oauth.descri: OAuth2 client-credentials authentication: the extension exchanges these for a short-lived bearer token. The optional `apiKey` and `virtualKey` companions are for gateways that check a second credential beside the bearer.
litellm.config.servers.auth.oauth.client: Client ID for the OAuth2 client-credentials grant.
OAuth client secret, inline. Omit to keep it in secret storage instead, or for public clients.
litellm.config.servers.auth.oauth.scopes: Space-separated scopes to request with the token. Leave out to request none.
litellm.config.servers.auth.oauth.apiKey: Optional companion API key sent as X-API-Key beside the OAuth bearer, inline. Omit to keep it in secret storage instead.
litellm.config.servers.auth.oauth.virtua: Optional companion key sent in its own header beside the OAuth bearer. Naming Authorization as the header hands it that header and skips the OAuth exchange.
litellm.config.servers.auth.virtualKey.d: A LiteLLM virtual key sent in a custom header instead of as a bearer token; use `apiKey` for gateways that take the key as an ordinary bearer.
litellm.config.servers.auth.virtualKey.h: Name of the header carrying the key, e.g. x-litellm-api-key.
litellm.config.servers.auth.virtualKey.v: The key sent in the header named above, inline. Omit to keep it in secret storage instead.
litellm.config.servers.headers.descripti: Custom HTTP headers sent on every request to this server (model discovery and chat completions): routing tags, tracing headers, additional gateway keys. Extension-managed auth headers win conflicts. Values are plain settings text; a truly secret value belongs in `auth`, which can live in secret storage.
litellm.config.servers.models.descriptio: Model configuration for this server only: `parameters` and `capabilities` mirror the global litellm-vscode-chat.models.* settings and apply above them, field by field.
litellm.config.servers.models.parameters: Request parameters for models served through this entry - the same shape as the global litellm-vscode-chat.models.parameters, scoped to this one entry. This is how to target one of two entries sharing a base URL. Where both settings match a model, the entry's parameters win key by key; runtime options and the model picker's per-model configuration override both.
litellm.config.servers.models.capabiliti: Capability overrides for models served through this entry - the same shape as the global litellm-vscode-chat.models.capabilities, scoped to this one entry. Where both settings match a model, the entry's fields win key by key.
litellm.config.servers.discovery.descrip: How model discovery treats this server: endpoints expected to fail, and model IDs to register when discovery cannot list them.
litellm.config.servers.discovery.expecte: Discovery endpoints expected to fail on this server: "modelListing" is GET /models, "modelInfo" is GET /model/info. A listed endpoint gets a single attempt (no retries) and its failure is logged as expected instead of counting as a server error. If the server lists no models at all, pair this with `discovery.declared`.
litellm.config.servers.discovery.declare: Exact model IDs to register even when discovery cannot list them. A declared ID is created only while discovery does not list it; once the server starts listing it, the declaration goes inert and the server's data takes over.
litellm.config.servers.budget.descriptio: Manual usage budget for this server, in USD. Used for budget bars and threshold alerts when the key reports no max_budget; when the key reports one too, this value wins and the key-reported budget is shown beside it.
litellm.config.servers.mcp.description: Make this server's MCP tools available in chat. `true` uses the server's own endpoint at `<baseUrl>/mcp`; the object form names another URL. The extension attaches this entry's credentials - API key, virtual key, or OAuth token - when the editor starts a session and never before, and only for an endpoint on this server's own origin.
litellm.config.servers.mcp.url.descripti: The MCP endpoint to publish for this server, when it is not `<baseUrl>/mcp`. Taken as written; leave it out to use the derived endpoint.
litellm.config.chat.promptCaching.descri: Enable prompt caching for supported models (currently Anthropic Claude). Places cache breakpoints on the tool definitions, the system prompt, the first user message, and the last text-bearing message of the conversation, so agent sessions reuse the cached prefix instead of re-paying for the whole history every turn. Only affects models that advertise prompt caching support.
litellm.config.models.parameters.descrip: Request parameters per model, keyed by matcher: an exact ID (`gpt-5`), a trailing-* glob (`gpt-5*`), a `/regex/` (whole-ID, optional `i` flag), or `*` for every model; the most specific match wins, and inheritance is opt-in via `_inheritable`/`_inherit_from`. Supports max_tokens, temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, stop, etc.; `_force` makes a record's fields beat runtime options and the model picker. To target one declared entry (two litellm-vscode-chat.servers entries can share a base URL), set the entry's `models.parameters` instead; entry records override this setting field by field. Only parameters you set are sent; the extension never injects defaults.
litellm.config.models.capabilities.descr: Corrections and additions to what LiteLLM reports a model can do - any `model_info` field. Core fields like `context_length`, `max_output_tokens`, and `supports_vision` drive registration and token limits; cost fields like `input_cost_per_token` drive pricing (your value beats the server's, and a 0/0 pair you write means genuinely free); fields the extension does not know are applied as overrides as-is. Keyed by the same matcher grammar as litellm-vscode-chat.models.parameters (exact ID, trailing-* glob, `/regex/`, or `*`), the most specific match winning. `_fallback` demotes a record's fields below the server's report; `_openrouter_model` fills unset capability fields (never pricing) from the bundled OpenRouter catalog. To create a model discovery cannot list, add its ID to a server entry's `discovery.declared`. These describe what a model can do; request parameters belong in litellm-vscode-chat.models.parameters.
Fill missing model capabilities from a bundled OpenRouter model catalog and refresh that catalog from openrouter.ai periodically (about weekly). Disable to stop the network refresh and the automatic matching; explicit _openrouter_model directives in models.capabilities keep working from the bundled snapshot.
litellm.config.ui.maskSecretInputs.descr: Mask secret input fields (API keys and other credentials) while typing in the dashboard. Disable to see the value as you type.
litellm.config.chat.timeout.description: Request timeout in milliseconds, bounding one chat completion call and the one-shot commit-message, pull-request-description, consult-tool, quick-fix and review-comment calls alike. Default is 300000ms (5 minutes). Increase this value if you're experiencing timeout errors with long-running requests.
litellm.config.chat.maxToolsPerRequest.d: How many tools one chat request may carry before the extension refuses it locally instead of sending it. Default is 128, the limit most OpenAI-compatible servers enforce. Raising it past what your server or model accepts moves the failure server-side: the request is sent and the server rejects it.
litellm.config.chat.additionalToolSchema: Extra JSON-Schema keywords to keep in tool input schemas, e.g. ["propertyNames"]. Tool schemas are sanitized to a built-in keyword allowlist before sending; keywords listed here are kept too, with their values passed through unchanged. The built-in set always applies. A keyword your server or model does not accept can make requests fail or degrade tool calling.
litellm.config.chat.tokenEstimation.desc: How prompt sizes are estimated for the local token budget before a request is sent. A loaded tokenizer keeps roughly 10-30 MB of token data in memory while active; the counting cost is negligible.
litellm.config.chat.tokenEstimation.auto: Script-aware estimate that loads the o200k_base tokenizer when the VS Code display language is not English, or when the chat contains enough text that plain character counting underestimates (CJK and other non-Latin scripts, emoji).
litellm.config.chat.tokenEstimation.heur: Plain 4-characters-per-token estimate. Never loads tokenizer data; undercounts CJK text roughly 4x.
litellm.config.chat.tokenEstimation.o200: Always load the o200k_base tokenizer (GPT-4o and newer models).
litellm.config.chat.tokenEstimation.cl10: Always load the cl100k_base tokenizer (GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 era models).
litellm.config.discovery.timeout.descrip: Request timeout in milliseconds for model discovery requests. Default is 30000ms (30 seconds).
litellm.config.discovery.cacheTtl.descri: How long, in milliseconds, discovered model lists are reused before the server is asked again. Default is 3600000 (1 hour). Higher values avoid repeated discovery requests when VS Code re-resolves providers in bursts, but models added or removed on the server take up to this long to appear; lower values pick up server-side changes sooner at the cost of more requests. Set to 0 to ask the server on every refresh (simultaneous refreshes still share one request). Run 'LiteLLM: Sync Models Now' to refresh immediately regardless of this setting.
litellm.config.discovery.staleServeWindo: How long, in milliseconds, a server that stops answering keeps serving its last known models, flagged stale, counted from its last successful discovery. Default is 600000 (10 minutes). Raise it if your server sleeps or restarts for longer and you want its models to stay in the picker meanwhile; set to 0 to never serve stale models, so a failed refresh empties that server's model list immediately.
litellm.config.usage.pollInterval.descri: How often, in milliseconds, per-server spend and budget data are refreshed from each LiteLLM server. Default is 300000 (5 minutes). Set to 0 to disable polling entirely (no background usage requests and no budget alerts); the 'LiteLLM: Refresh Usage Now' command and the dashboard still fetch on demand.
litellm.config.usage.initialRefreshDelay: How long, in milliseconds, after extension startup the first usage poll runs. Default is 5000 (5 seconds).
litellm.config.usage.serversChangeRefres: How long, in milliseconds, after a change to the servers setting usage data is refreshed. Default is 2000 (2 seconds), long enough to coalesce a burst of settings.json keystrokes.
litellm.config.usage.pollingOffFreshness: How long, in milliseconds, on-demand usage data counts as fresh while polling is off (usage.pollInterval 0). Default is 600000 (10 minutes). While polling is on, the freshness window is twice the poll interval instead. Set to 0 to never count usage data as fresh while polling is off, which hides the usage status-bar item.
litellm.config.usage.alertThresholds.des: Budget fractions that trigger a usage alert, each above 0 and at most 1. Default is [0.8, 0.95]: alert at 80% and 95% of a server's effective budget. An empty array disables threshold alerts.
litellm.config.usage.statusBar.descripti: When the usage status-bar item is shown: "always", "alerts-only" (only while a server has crossed a budget alert threshold), or "off".
litellm.config.usage.currencySymbol.desc: Prefix on every spend and price figure, e.g. "EUR ". Display only: amounts are never converted - they render exactly as the server reports them. An empty string shows bare numbers.
litellm.config.ui.theme.description: How the dashboard picks its colors. Auto follows the VS Code theme you are using, including high contrast.
litellm.config.ui.accent.description: The accent color the dashboard uses for primary buttons, selection, focus, and links. Status colors are unaffected.
litellm.config.inlineCompletions.enabled: Opt in to inline (ghost text) completions from a LiteLLM model. Off by default; nothing is registered and no requests are sent until enabled, the one exception being the dashboard's explicit "Test model" button. The feature stays idle until `#litellm-vscode-chat.inlineCompletions.model#` names a model.
litellm.config.inlineCompletions.model.d: The model that serves inline completions, e.g. `{ "server": "Team proxy", "model": "gpt-4o-mini" }`: the label of a `#litellm-vscode-chat.servers#` entry plus one of its raw model IDs. `null` means no model is picked and the feature stays idle.
litellm.config.inlineCompletions.languag: Where inline completions run, e.g. `{ "mode": "block", "languages": ["markdown"] }` runs them everywhere except markdown. Mode `"block"` runs completions everywhere except the listed exact VS Code language IDs; `"allow"` runs them only there (empty list: nowhere).
"block" runs completions everywhere except the listed languages; "allow" runs them only there.
Exact VS Code language IDs, e.g. "typescript".
Opt in to commit message generation from a LiteLLM model. Off by default; the command stays hidden and no requests are sent until enabled, and the feature stays idle until `#litellm-vscode-chat.commitGeneration.model#` names a model.
litellm.config.commitGeneration.model.de: The model that drafts commit messages, e.g. `{ "server": "Team proxy", "model": "gpt-4o-mini" }`: the label of a `#litellm-vscode-chat.servers#` entry plus one of its raw model IDs. `null` means no model is picked and the feature stays idle.
litellm.config.commitGeneration.prompt.d: Custom instruction for the generated commit message, replacing the built-in instruction wholesale. Empty uses the built-in (a Conventional Commits subject plus a short body).
litellm.config.featureModel.server.descr: The label of the servers entry that serves the model.
litellm.config.featureModel.model.descri: The raw model ID as that server reports it.
litellm.config.prGeneration.enabled.desc: Opt in to pull request title and description generation from a LiteLLM model. Off by default; the command stays hidden and no requests are sent until enabled, the one exception being the dashboard's explicit "Test model" button. The feature stays idle until `#litellm-vscode-chat.prGeneration.model#` names a model.
litellm.config.prGeneration.model.descri: The model that drafts PR descriptions, e.g. `{ "server": "Team proxy", "model": "gpt-4o-mini" }`: the label of a `#litellm-vscode-chat.servers#` entry plus one of its raw model IDs. `null` means no model is picked and the feature stays idle.
litellm.config.consultTool.enabled.descr: Opt in to the consult tool, which lets a chat agent ask a second LiteLLM model for its opinion while it works. Off by default; nothing is registered and no requests are sent until enabled, the one exception being the dashboard's explicit "Test model" button. The tool stays unregistered until `#litellm-vscode-chat.consultTool.model#` names a model. Once both are set, the agent decides when to consult, without asking you first.
litellm.config.consultTool.model.descrip: The model the consult tool asks, e.g. `{ "server": "Team proxy", "model": "gpt-4o-mini" }`: the label of a `#litellm-vscode-chat.servers#` entry plus one of its raw model IDs. `null` means no model is picked and the feature stays idle.
litellm.config.quickFix.enabled.descript: Show Fix and Explain quick fixes on diagnostics. Both open the chat view and SEND the question to the `@litellm` participant, with the diagnostics and the lines they sit on attached; when the chat view cannot answer, they fall back to the model below and write the answer to a new markdown editor.
litellm.config.quickFix.model.descriptio: The model behind the quick-fix fallback path, e.g. `{ "server": "Team proxy", "model": "gpt-4o-mini" }`: the label of a `#litellm-vscode-chat.servers#` entry plus one of its raw model IDs. `null` means no model is picked and the fallback stays idle.
litellm.config.reviewComments.enabled.de: Opt in to AI review comments on your changes from a LiteLLM model. Off by default; no comment threads exist and no review is sent until enabled, the one exception being the dashboard's explicit "Test model" button. The feature stays idle until `#litellm-vscode-chat.reviewComments.model#` names a model.
litellm.config.reviewComments.model.desc: The model that writes review comments, e.g. `{ "server": "Team proxy", "model": "gpt-4o-mini" }`: the label of a `#litellm-vscode-chat.servers#` entry plus one of its raw model IDs. `null` means no model is picked and the feature stays idle.
litellm.config.chatParticipant.enabled.d: The @litellm chat participant. On by default and costs nothing until invoked; it answers with the chat request's own model.
litellm.participant.description: Ask your own LiteLLM models, answered by whichever model the chat model picker has selected.
litellm.participant.sampleRequest: Which models do my LiteLLM servers offer?
litellm.participant.disambiguation.catal: The user is asking which models their own LiteLLM servers currently serve, or about one of those models' context window, tool support, or image support. Not about a vendor's public model line-up.
Which models do I have connected right now?
What context window does the model on my local proxy have?
litellm.participant.disambiguation.ownMo: The user wants this question answered by a model from their own LiteLLM proxy rather than the built-in chat model, usually saying so explicitly.
Ask my own model to explain this function.
Answer this with my LiteLLM model instead of the default one.

litellm.participant.command.explain.disa: The user wants to understand what a diagnostic on their code means and why the editor is reporting it here.
What does this TypeScript error actually mean?
